phases.name: P0 validated commit boundary
phases.description: Stop Invalid Date reaching state, restore the last valid date, and commit once per completed edit.

steps.name: Add isValidDate predicate
criteria: isValidDate returns true only for a Date whose getTime is not NaN
Rejects null, undefined, strings, numbers and an Invalid Date
Narrows the type to Date for TypeScript callers
steps.implementation_notes: New file beside localDate.ts. One named predicate so the same check cannot be written three subtly different ways. Invalid Date is truthy, which is why every ad-hoc falsy guard in this codebase fails against it.

steps.name: DateRangeSelector becomes validated commit boundary
criteria: Typing 0 into the day or month section never calls the parent with an invalid date
After an invalid keystroke the committed date still equals the previous prop
Typing a full date then blurring calls the parent exactly once
A completed out-of-range date is rejected and the previous value stands
A pending valid draft is flushed when the component unmounts
steps.implementation_notes: Draft state seeded from props, resynced by effect on prop change. onChange updates the draft only. Commit from slotProps.textField.onBlur and from the calendar onAccept, through a guard: isValidDate AND within [minDate,maxDate] AND different from the committed prop; on failure reset the draft to the prop. Flush a pending valid draft in a useEffect cleanup, because the selector is mounted inside a Popover that unmounts on close and blur-on-unmount is not guaranteed (risk R2). The new describe block must NOT mock @mui/x-date-pickers; pin the format with the existing _testLocalDateFormat prop and address sections by aria-label Day/Month/Year (their role is spinbutton, so getAllByRole textbox finds nothing). The two existing tests at lines 91-121 encode the removed behaviour and must be rewritten against the commit-on-blur contract, never preserved by changing the component back.

steps.name: Popover close still commits a valid entry
criteria: Entering a valid date then closing the popover calls the parent handler once
Existing DashboardHeader tests stay green
steps.implementation_notes: Mount the real DateRangeSelector rather than the module stub at line 5 for this one case. Guards risk R2: a silently lost edit is worse than the bug being fixed. No production change expected here; if one proves necessary it belongs in 01-02.

phases.name: P1 defence in depth
phases.description: Close the remaining sinks an invalid date can reach.

steps.name: Guard the BaseMetricsView date handlers
criteria: An invalid date passed to either handler leaves state and URL params unchanged
The Bug 5566 local-midnight cases stay green
steps.implementation_notes: Replace the falsy guard with an isValidDate guard at lines 1224-1234, in both handlers. This is the last line before state, so no future caller of these handlers can reintroduce the crash.

steps.name: Cache keys stop using toISOString
criteria: Each key names the local calendar day rather than a UTC instant
The key is stable for a viewer whose local day differs from the UTC day
Existing cache-key tests stay green
steps.implementation_notes: All three build a day key from a UTC instant during render and therefore throw exactly as the range label does. Switch to formatLocalDate. blockedTrend.ts was NOT in the original analysis, which named only the two hooks: step 02-01's failing test reached it at line 67 through BaseMetricsView line 1854, proving it is a live sink on the same path. Keying a local calendar window by its UTC instant is the same latent mismatch already fixed everywhere else in this dashboard. The date-typed inputs elsewhere in the app (ThroughputQuickSetting, FlowMetricsConfigurationComponent, ForecastSettingsComponent) share the UTC day-shift class but are NOT crash paths, because a native date input emits either an empty string or a complete date; leave them alone.

steps.name: formatLocalDate refuses an invalid date
criteria: formatLocalDate throws on an invalid date instead of returning NaN-NaN-NaN
The message names the offending input
Every existing caller stays green
steps.implementation_notes: MUST land after 01-02 and 02-01 or it moves the crash rather than removing it. Turns silent URL and query-string corruption into a loud, test-visible failure, matching the rigour parseLocalDate already applies at lines 29-34.

phases.name: P2 belt and braces, dead code
phases.description: A label is never worth an application crash, and dead code carrying a live bug is worse than dead code.

steps.name: DashboardHeader label never throws
criteria: An invalid date renders a placeholder instead of unmounting the app
A valid date renders unchanged as dd MMM yyyy
steps.implementation_notes: formatDate at line 50 calls the date-fns format, which throws RangeError during render and unmounts the tree into AppErrorBoundary. Nothing invalid can reach it once phases 01 and 02 land, but a label is never worth a crash.

steps.name: Delete the unused DatePickerComponent
criteria: Component and its test are gone
No import of it remains anywhere in src
Build and full frontend suite stay green
steps.implementation_notes: Nothing imports it but its own test. Its guard rejects only a falsy value and a future date, and dayjs(invalid).isAfter(dayjs()) is false, so an invalid Dayjs passes straight through: the identical defect in the dayjs dialect. Confirm the grep across src before deleting.
